name: gooey-text
title: Gooey Text
description: Words that melt into each other: two blurred copies cross-fade and an SVG threshold filter merges their edges into one gooey shape.
author: Victor Welander <https://21st.dev/@victorwelander>
docs:
Installed `GooeyText` in `components/ui/`, plus `useReducedMotion` in `hooks/`. Render it inside a box with a height: `
`. The words are absolutely positioned and centered on the root, which has no height of its own. Two copies of the text cross-fade while their blur grows and shrinks, and an SVG color matrix (alpha x 255 - 140) thresholds the result, so the blurred edges merge into one gooey shape. Set the size and color with `textClassName` (default: `text-6xl`, `text-[60pt]` from md up, `text-foreground`). It is a different technique from Text Morph, which glides shared characters to their new places. Screen readers read the full list once (or `label`); the morphing copies are hidden from them. Under reduced motion the words just swap. Like upstream, the text is empty until the first morph (`cooldownTime`); set `renderFirstWordOnServer` to put the first word in the server render instead, which keeps the server HTML and no-JavaScript visits from showing an empty box. Ported from Victor Welander's 21st.dev item "Gooey Text Morphing" (MIT, copyright 2024 Victor Welander): https://21st.dev/@victorwelander/components/gooey-text-morphing. The license text is in the file.
